title: Recognising and representing patterns and relationships by finding an algebraic expression for the nth term
summary: Find and verify nth-term rules for arithmetic sequences and growing linear patterns using the common difference and constant adjustment.
objectives: Recognise when a numerical or visual pattern has a constant first difference.
Form an nth-term rule dn + c from the common difference and a known term.
Verify a rule against several terms and use it to find or test term positions.

sections.title: From common difference to nth term

blocks.text: An arithmetic sequence changes by the same amount from one term to the next. That common difference d becomes the coefficient of n in a linear nth-term rule. Start with dn, compare its first value d with the actual first term, and add the constant adjustment c.

For 5, 8, 11, 14, … the common difference is 3. The trial rule 3n starts 3, 6, 9, 12, which is always 2 too small, so Tₙ = 3n + 2. The position n begins at 1 unless the problem explicitly defines a stage 0.

sections.title: Worked example: use two later terms

prompt.text: A linear sequence has third term 14 and eighth term 39. Find its nth term.

content.text: Five term intervals separate positions 3 and 8, so find the change per interval.
Use Tₙ = 5n + c and substitute the third term.

sections.verification_note: The rule gives T₃ = 15 − 1 = 14 and T₈ = 40 − 1 = 39, matching both pieces of information.

sections.title: Count what is fixed and what grows

blocks.text: A visual pattern can also be linear. Separate a fixed starting part from a group added at every new stage. If stage 1 has 6 sticks and each later stage shares one side while adding 5 sticks, the total is 6 + 5(n − 1). Simplifying gives the same dn + c form used for a number sequence.

The coefficient 5 describes the growth per stage. The constant 1 is an adjustment determined by the starting arrangement; it does not necessarily count a visible group by itself. Draw or tabulate the first few stages before deciding which part repeats.

sections.title: Worked example: model joined pentagons

prompt.text: Stage 1 is one pentagon made from 5 sticks. Each new pentagon shares one side with the previous pentagon. Find the rule and the number of sticks at stage 12.

content.text: The first pentagon contributes 5 sticks; each of the remaining n − 1 pentagons adds 4.
Expand and simplify the nth-term rule.

sections.verification_note: The first three values from the rule are 5, 9 and 13, matching the construction’s increase of 4 sticks per stage.

blocks.text: A constant first difference supports a linear rule; changing first differences require another model. Do not write “first term plus the difference times n” because that counts one extra increase. The safe form is first term + (n − 1) differences, which simplifies to dn + c.

Check at least two known positions, including n = 1. To decide whether a value belongs to a sequence, set Tₙ equal to that value and solve for n. It is a term only if the solution is an allowed positive whole-number position.

feedback.text: The common difference is 4, and 4(1) needs 2 more to make the first term 6.

blocks.text: Confirm a constant first difference, use it as the coefficient of n, and find the constant adjustment from a known term. For visual patterns, separate the initial structure from the repeated growth. Verify the rule at n = 1 and another known position before using it to predict or test a term.
